findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the long-path fixture to pad so that len(cwd) + len('<sha>^:<ticket>/<event>.json') > 260 while cwd alone stays under 260, and record that the test fails (RED) against the old `git show` code on the Windows dispatch.
evidence: 'On Windows only, it restores a deleted source under a cwd padded past MAX_PATH. The real restore must return the file.'
Root cause: 'cwd plus that argument exceeds MAX_PATH'
findings.finding: The Windows long-path fixture is underspecified. 'a cwd padded past MAX_PATH' could mean the cwd alone exceeds 260 characters. In that case directory creation, chdir, or git itself may fail for reasons unrelated to the `<sha>^:<path>` ambiguity stat. The test could then error before reaching the fixed code, or pass and fail for the wrong reason. The plan also does not say the test was confirmed RED against the old `git show` code.
scenarios: On the runner, the padded cwd itself exceeds 260 chars, so the repo setup step fails (or needs core.longpaths) and the test errors regardless of the fix.
The padding is too short, so the test passes on both the old and the new code and guards nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Pad the tmp dir so that len(cwd) + len('<40-hex>^:' + relpath) exceeds 260 while len(cwd) < 248. Confirm RED once by running the test against the unfixed `git show` code on the tmp-branch dispatch, and record the run id.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Windows long-path test, compute the padding so len(cwd)+len(rev-arg) > 260 while len(cwd)+len(longest repo-internal path) < 260, do not set core.longpaths, and assert as a precondition that `git show <sha>^:<path>` in that cwd exits 128 with 'Filename too long' before asserting that the restore returns the file.
evidence: Plan: "On Windows only, it restores a deleted source under a cwd padded past MAX_PATH. The real restore must return the file."
Root cause §1: "cwd plus that argument exceeds MAX_PATH" — the argument is about 42 chars longer than the on-disk relative path, so the window that triggers the bug is narrow
No step checks that the old `git show <sha>^:<path>` fails with 'Filename too long' in the test's setup
findings.finding: The Windows-only test says to restore 'under a cwd padded past MAX_PATH', which does not pin down the failing condition precisely. The bug fires only when cwd + the revision argument (`<40-hex>^:<ticket>/<event>.json`) is longer than MAX_PATH while git's own repo paths (`.git/objects/xx/…`, `<ticket>/<event>.json`) stay under it. If the cwd itself is past MAX_PATH, `git init`/`commit`/checkout in the fixture fail before the restore runs (core.longpaths is off by default, which is why the bug reproduces on the runner). If the padding is too short, the test passes even with the old `git show`. The plan has no step confirming the test actually hits the bug's condition.
findings.location: Approach → New regression test tests/unit/test_fsck_restore_long_path.py (second bullet)
scenarios: The padding is chosen too short: the Windows test passes on both the old and new code and proves nothing.

The padding is chosen too long, so the cwd itself exceeds MAX_PATH: fixture setup errors on Windows, the test fails or gets deselected, and it pushes toward setting core.longpaths, which would hide the bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the tmp repo under a padded directory whose length is computed from the actual rev-arg length (e.g. pad = 261 - len(rev_arg) - len(base) + small margin, and check that cwd + longest worktree/.git path stays < 260). Before calling `restore_deleted_sources`, run `git show <sha>^:<path>` directly and assert returncode 128 with 'Filename too long' in stderr (or pytest.skip if the precondition can't be built), then assert the restore returns and writes the `.retired` file.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the long-path test padding as cwd < MAX_PATH but len(cwd) + len(f"{sha}^:{path}") > MAX_PATH, and add a negative-control assertion that `git show <sha>^:<path>` exits 128 under that same padding.
evidence: Plan: 'On Windows only, it restores a deleted source under a cwd padded past MAX_PATH.'

findings.finding: The Windows-only regression test pads the cwd past MAX_PATH. The reproduced failure is different: the cwd itself was under MAX_PATH and only cwd plus the `<sha>^:<path>` argument went over. With a cwd longer than MAX_PATH, git or CreateProcess can fail before any object lookup, so the test can fail even after the fix. The test also has no negative control showing `git show` fails under the same padding, so it can pass without proving anything.
findings.location: Approach — New regression test, tests/unit/test_fsck_restore_long_path.py (Windows-only bullet)
scenarios: The cwd is padded to more than 260 characters. Spawning git, or git's startup getcwd/chdir, fails with 'Filename too long' or 'directory name is invalid'. The test is red with the fix in place.
The padding is too short to trigger the stat failure. The test passes, but it would also pass without the fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Pad the tmp repo path so the cwd is about 200–240 characters, and size the ticket or event path so cwd plus the revision argument goes past 260. First assert that `run_git(tracker, 'show', f'{sha}^:{path}', check=False).returncode != 0` (the precondition reproduces). Then assert that `restore_deleted_sources` returns the file.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the Windows regression test pads cwd so that cwd + `<sha>^:<ticket>/<event>.json` exceeds MAX_PATH while cwd itself stays within it. Add a precondition assertion that `git show <sha>^:<path>` fails with 'Filename too long' at that padding before asserting the cat-file restore succeeds.
evidence: 'On Windows only, it restores a deleted source under a cwd padded past MAX_PATH. The real restore must return the file.'
Root cause: 'Under the sweep's pytest temp dir, cwd plus that argument exceeds MAX_PATH.'
'It asserts that both `fsck_restore` reads use `cat-file blob` and never `git show <rev>:<path>`, by spying on `run_git`'
findings.finding: The Windows-only regression test is specified as restoring 'under a cwd padded past MAX_PATH'. The root cause is that cwd PLUS the `<sha>^:<path>` argument exceeds MAX_PATH, not the cwd alone. A cwd that itself exceeds MAX_PATH can make subprocess/CreateProcess or git fail for unrelated reasons, so the test may error or pass for the wrong reason. The plan also has no guard that the chosen padding actually reproduces the old failure. Without one, the test can pass vacuously on a runner where the padding does not trigger the stat error. This test is the only behavioral coverage of the product fix: the spy test only checks argv, and Linux cannot reproduce the bug.
scenarios: The padding makes the cwd itself exceed MAX_PATH. Repo setup or the git subprocess fails before restore runs, so the test errors or gets skipped instead of proving the fix.

The padding is too short on the runner. `git show` would also have succeeded, so the test goes green without ever exercising the long-path condition, and a future revert to `git show` would not be caught on Windows.
findings.suggested_fix: In test_fsck_restore_long_path.py (Windows branch), compute the padding from len(cwd) + len(rev_arg) > 260 with len(cwd) < 260. First run `git show <sha>^:<path>` with check=False and assert returncode == 128 and 'Filename too long' in stderr (the reproduction guard), then call the real restore and assert the file is returned.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the source of per-test pass evidence (e.g., add `-rA` or `--junitxml` with an uploaded artifact to the sweep-windows pytest command, or run the 11 node ids explicitly with `-rA` in the validation run), and add test.yml to Scope if the command changes.
evidence: test.yml:281-283: `uv run --no-sync pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q -p no:cacheprovider ...` (no -rA, no --junitxml, no artifact upload)
Plan: 'record the run id and per-test outcomes in a comment'
AC1: 'Every line removed from store-history.args names a test that passed in a sweep (windows) run on main'
Evidence class: Contradicted. The CI surface as configured does not emit named pass outcomes.
findings.finding: The validation and AC1 evidence depend on reading per-test pass outcomes from a `sweep (windows)` run. That job runs pytest with `-q` and no `-rA` or junit artifact, so passing tests never appear by name in the log. A test that was skipped or not collected cannot be told apart from one that passed.
findings.location: Testing — Pre-merge Windows validation; Acceptance Criteria AC1
scenarios: One of the 11 tests is skipped on Windows (e.g. by a platform skipif) or not collected after a rename. The -q log shows no failure, and the line is removed even though the test never passed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `-rA` to the sweep-windows pytest invocation in .github/workflows/test.yml, which prints a 'PASSED <nodeid>' line for each test, and list test.yml unconditionally in Scope. Alternatively, record the evidence from a dispatch whose log shows each node id as PASSED.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the spy test reach the `_uuid_fallback` read as well, e.g. monkeypatch `fsck_restore._deleted_history` to return `{}` (or call `_uuid_fallback` directly with an empty `have`), and assert that each of the two reads issues `cat-file blob`.
evidence: Plan: "It asserts that both `fsck_restore` reads use `cat-file blob` ... by spying on `run_git` while restoring a deleted source in a tmp repo."
fsck_restore.py:99-100: `if name in have or name + RETIRED_SUFFIX in have: continue` comes before the line-104 run_git call
fsck_restore.py:135: the main pass runs first and adds restored names; the fallback only covers uuids the directory walk missed (history simplification), which a simple tmp repo does not produce
findings.finding: The spy test is described as asserting that BOTH fsck_restore reads use `cat-file blob` 'while restoring a deleted source in a tmp repo'. A single ordinary restore never reaches the `_uuid_fallback` read. Once `restore_deleted_sources` restores the file, the name is in `have`. `_uuid_fallback` then hits `continue` before calling run_git, or `snapshot_missing_sources` no longer lists the uuid. So the second site (line 104) is never checked, and a regression there would go unnoticed.
findings.location: Approach → New regression test tests/unit/test_fsck_restore_long_path.py (first bullet)
scenarios: Someone later reverts only `_uuid_fallback` to `git show <rev>:<path>`. The spy test still passes because that code path never runs, and the deep-path bug comes back for fallback-restored sources.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the spy assertion into two cases. (1) A normal `restore_deleted_sources` run checks the main-pass read. (2) Monkeypatch `rebar._commands.fsck_restore._deleted_history` to return `{}` so the restore falls through to `_uuid_fallback`, then check that its run_git call is `('cat-file', 'blob', f'{commit}^:{path}')` and that no call uses `show`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default for a test that still fails on the Windows validation run: remove all 11 lines, dispatch, re-add any failing line, and stop to re-investigate (do not mark it unsupported) unless a Windows-inherent reason is shown.
evidence: 'remove each line whose test passes in the Windows validation run'
Testing: 'on the exact fixed tree with the lines removed from the args file'
AC2: 'each remaining line names a test recorded on this ticket as intentionally unsupported on Windows with the reason'
findings.finding: The plan does not say what happens if any of the 11 tests still fails in the pre-merge Windows validation run. Root cause claims all 11 are fixed, and AC2 only permits remaining lines that are 'intentionally unsupported on Windows'. Neither the Approach nor AC2 says whether a still-failing test means further investigation, a new ticket, or a classification as unsupported. The order of steps is also implicit: remove all lines, dispatch, then re-add any failures.
scenarios: One test fails on the dispatch run for an unrelated, flaky reason. The executor must decide alone whether to re-add the line and either label it 'unsupported' or stop.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach: 'Remove all 11 lines, then dispatch. If any test fails, restore its line and treat the ticket as not done: re-investigate. Mark it unsupported only with a Windows-inherent reason recorded in a comment.'

Both ACs only concern the deselect file. The product fix, including the real-user `rebar store fsck --repair-snapshots` symptom, and the regression guard are proven only indirectly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] When `git cat-file blob` exits nonzero in fsck_restore, surface the exit code and stderr (a warning in the repair output) instead of silently skipping the blob.
evidence: 'Same bytes, same `check=False` / `text=False` handling.'
'Git dies with `fatal: failed to stat ...` (exit 128), so the blob is skipped and nothing is restored.'
findings.finding: The fix keeps `check=False` and the existing skip-on-failure behavior. A git failure while reading a pre-image therefore still silently skips the blob and restores nothing. That silent skip is why this bug was hard to diagnose (exit 128 with 'Filename too long' was swallowed). The other `git show` sites remain exposed, so the same swallowing will recur until comic-heavyset-jerboa lands.
findings.location: Approach: src/rebar/_commands/fsck_restore.py bullet; Root cause item 1
scenarios: A different git error (corrupt object, missing parent commit) makes `--repair-snapshots` report success while silently restoring nothing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Allow AC1 evidence from a `workflow_dispatch` of test.yml on main right after merge (or state the schedule cadence), so closure does not wait on the scheduler.
evidence: 'the first scheduled `test.yml` run on main whose head contains the merge commit'
findings.finding: AC1's evidence is gated on 'the first scheduled `test.yml` run on main' after merge. The schedule cadence is not stated, so the ticket cannot close in-session at merge time, and its closure depends on an external schedule.
scenarios: The schedule is weekly, or the scheduled run is skipped or cancelled, so the ticket sits open long after the fix lands.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the AC1 evidence to: 'the first `sweep (windows)` run of test.yml on main whose head contains the merge commit, triggered by `gh workflow run 294845723 --ref main` immediately after merge (or the next scheduled run, whichever comes first)'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Dispatch by workflow file name (`gh workflow run test.yml --ref tmp/b4-cold-censorable-armedcrab`), or record the `gh workflow list` output showing 294845723 is test.yml.
evidence: The repo-wide search for '294845723' finds only a plan-review cache file, with no mapping to .github/workflows/test.yml.
Evidence class: Unverified. `gh workflow run` accepts an id or a workflow file name, but this particular id was not confirmed against `gh workflow list`.
findings.finding: The dispatch command uses the hard-coded numeric workflow id `294845723`. Nothing in the repo maps that id to test.yml, so if it names another workflow, the validation dispatches the wrong pipeline.
scenarios: The id belongs to a different workflow, or test.yml was re-created and got a new id. The dispatch then runs a pipeline without the sweep (windows) job and produces no Windows evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `gh workflow run 294845723 --ref ...` with `gh workflow run test.yml --ref tmp/b4-cold-censorable-armedcrab`.
